Ethereum Postpones Glamsterdam Upgrade on Hoodi Testnet Over EIP-8037 Compatibility Concerns According to the Ethereum Foundation, Ethereum core developers have postponed the Glamsterdam upgrade on the Hoodi testnet, originally scheduled for October 26, to further investigate compatibility concerns between EIP-8037's gas accounting changes and existing mainnet smart contracts. The planned increase of Hoodi's gas limit to 200 million has also been canceled. Node operators must update their clients to prevent activation of the fork as originally scheduled. New dates for the Hoodi upgrade and mainnet activation have not yet been determined. — link

Spot Bitcoin ETFs Recorded $635M in Net Outflows on October 22 On October 22 (ET), spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded total net outflows of $635M, led by BlackRock’s IBIT with $254M. Spot Ethereum ETFs recorded total net outflows of $111M, led by BlackRock’s ETHA with $75.45M. — link

Highlight Clip: Arthur Hayes: HYPE Could Significantly Underperform ETH and ZEC Arthur Hayes: HYPE Could Significantly Underperform ETH and ZEC On October 16, BitMEX founder Arthur Hayes stated that Hyperliquid has demonstrated genuine demand for on-chain perpetual futures markets. However, as the sector has become a consensus trade, HYPE's risk-reward appeal has declined. Hayes believes the main risk of investing in HYPE is not necessarily losing money, but potentially significantly underperforming other crypto assets such as ETH and ZEC. He noted that perpetual DEXs are facing increasingly intense competition as their offerings become more homogeneous. While he recognizes the Hyperliquid team's achievements and is willing to use its products as a consumer, he does not want to participate as an investor. Previously, Hayes publicly set a $150 price target for HYPE, but announced that he had sold all his HYPE and NEAR holdings just days later. WuBlockchain reminds readers that Arthur Hayes has a relatively low historical accuracy rate in market predictions and frequently revises his views. Readers are advised to focus on his analytical framework rather than specific price targets and timing forecasts. — link

Kimchi Token’s Market Cap Plunges Over 98% to $284K After Pumpfun Co-Founder Removes Repost Crypto trader Kimchi posted a promotional image this morning with a QR code linking to a new memecoin, Project Kimchi. After Pumpfun co-founder Alon reposted it, the token’s market cap briefly reached approximately $15M. Alon subsequently removed his repost, while Kimchi deleted the original post and removed “pumpfun” from his bio. The token’s price then fell sharply. Alon had previously described Kimchi as the first trader to truly bridge crypto and pop culture. Neither has publicly explained the deleted post or removed repost. According to GMGN, the token’s market cap is now approximately $284K, down over 98% from its peak, with around $9.3M in 24-hour trading volume. — link
